answer: Think of signed falconer licence with wildlife agency attestation as a toll booth: a licence the wildlife agency issued after husbandry exams and inspection, so the pearl of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The velvet is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The trellis is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
